# V2 evaluation method review

Reviewed 6 November 2026. This is a protocol recommendation, not a V2 recovery result. Authority for die-a-rea behavior is the locally inspected checkout at `0d322552673309372f9937bc5f0c50641ed1514e`; this review does not substitute current `main` for that pin. The public upstream identities were checked against [danihelenterprises/die-a-rea](https://github.com/danihelenterprises/die-a-rea) and [morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea). REA identifies `rea-agents` as its npm package; the lab pins 6.8.0, javascript-obfuscator 5.10.0 and Next.js 16.4.5 in [package.json](../package.json).

## Decision

Use **the pinned tool's default High profile, with its full default randomization and tarpit settings, its default authorization notice and an available JavaScript adapter** for the primary V2 hardened arm. Preserve an original V2 arm from the same application build. Measure behavior recovered and resources spent separately. A Paranoid or custom-engine experiment can be an additional arm, with its actual options recorded; changing the profile name is insufficient evidence of stronger JavaScript protection. These recommendations follow the actual [profile resolution][policy], [manifest defaults][manifest] and [adapter call path][host].

The relevant threat is analysis of possessed artifact bytes on an analyst-controlled host. Upstream explicitly assumes runtime checks can be patched and seeks to raise recovery cost. Thus copied server artifacts and public browser/API access must remain separate access conditions. Neither a high static score nor a failed bounded attempt demonstrates that recovery is impossible. [Threat model][threat]

## Actual enabled configuration

The following values are the defaults at the pin; setting them explicitly makes the experiment easier to audit. `High` is the manifest profile default, although the lower-level `ResolvedPolicy::default()` by itself is Low. [Policy][policy] [Manifest][manifest]

```toml
[policy]
profile = "high"

[randomization]
enabled = true
seed = 20261106 # recorded experiment seed; default 0 derives a seed
junk_density = 0.35
decoy_functions = 200
decoy_strings = 500
decoy_files = 25
depth_bomb = 3

[tarpit]
enabled = true
padding_kb = 128
max_total_kb = 4096
prompt_gate = true
honeypots = 25
custom_payloads = []

[verify]
js_syntax = true
```

Omit `agent_defense.notice_text` to retain the seeded upstream gate text. High generates a canary without an explicit list. Post-build verification is an additional health check, not a stronger protection. [Notice/canary resolution][build] [Gate text][canary] [Health checks][health]

The effective single-file JavaScript lane is:

| Layer | Actual behavior to record |
| --- | --- |
| Built-in text processing | Whole-line source-map/comment removal, notice and canary comments, then generated noise and the runtime marker. |
| Randomization | 200 functions, 500 strings and three depth structures of depth 3. `decoy_files` applies to directory targets; it does not produce 25 sibling files for a single-file target. `junk_density` is not consumed by this JS generation path. |
| Tarpit | Before external obfuscation: 25 honeypots and approximately 128 KiB of comment padding per file, plus a live notice literal. The 4096 KiB setting caps padding, not every category of generated bytes. |
| External engine | Compact output; control-flow flattening enabled at threshold 0.5; string arrays with base64 encoding at threshold 0.75; engine dead-code injection disabled. The built-in decoy functions still exist independently. |
| Runtime | High appends an observational JS guard; it does not block execution. |

Sources: [single-file generation and tree generation][generation], [adapter engine options][js], [JS runtime source][guard]. Base64 here is encoding, so describe the actual setting rather than promising cryptographic secrecy.

**Generated noise is not necessarily retained noise.** The external adapter runs after built-in padding generation. A local probe on installed javascript-obfuscator 5.10.0 using the adapter's exact seven engine settings removed an ordinary `/* ANALYST NOTICE: benchmark-padding-marker */` comment; the marker was absent from output. The probe's live string marker was also absent as plaintext, consistent with string encoding. Thus enabling 128 KiB padding does not establish that 128 KiB survives the complete stock JS lane. Record final bytes and distinguish generated counts from retained material. The build metadata retains `injected` counts from before the external adapter but measures total bytes afterward, so the analysis-noise fraction can overstate retained noise. [Generation/adapter order and metadata assembly][build]

Do not translate policy switches into claims unsupported by the JS implementation. The host forwards the resolved policy but supplies only `{ "out": destination }` in adapter options; the adapter reads its own fixed options and does not translate policy fields. High and Paranoid therefore use the same engine settings on this path. Paranoid additionally enables generated analyst-decoy comments, but its `pack` and data-flow switches do not implement JS packing or stronger engine flattening here. Likewise High's `anti_debug` and `integrity_selfcheck` flags do not establish separate active JS blocking or integrity enforcement. [Host adapter invocation][host] [Adapter][js] [Profile differences][policy] [Generated decoy notes][generation]

The build seed governs the Rust-generated material but is **not forwarded to the JavaScript engine**. That engine's seed defaults to 0, documented as unseeded. Freeze actual artifact bytes, per-file SHA-256, lockfile and tool/binary hashes. A claim that `--seed` alone reproduces the final obfuscated bytes would be unsupported. If deterministic engine seeding is added, label and retain that adapter patch separately from the stock-default arm. [Host request][host] [Engine seed documentation][engine-doc]

## Gate and runtime interpretation

The prompt gate creates an ordinary `var` holding the notice, conditional on notice enabled, tarpit enabled and `prompt_gate=true`. The notice is also carried in comments/padding. This is text an analyst may encounter, not a request handler, authentication check or execution barrier. Subsequent engine processing can encode a string and remove comments, so inspect the final bytes/decoded material before claiming which notices reach REA or the model. [Generation][generation] [Adapter options][js]

The experiment owner should provide the same explicit authorization to both recovery arms and retain the default artifact notice. Record refusals or authorization clarification separately from technical recovery failures; an instruction-following stop does not establish algorithmic resistance. The former custom text, “Authorized educational reverse-engineering benchmark,” changes the gate's meaning and should not stand in for the default-notice test. [Existing manifest](../die-a-rea.toml) [Default gate variants][canary]

The embedded JS guard checks `NODE_OPTIONS` containing `--inspect`, `FRIDA`, and the React DevTools global hook. It writes `globalThis.__DIREA_GUARD__` and invokes an optional operator hook inside a catch. It has no blocking behavior by default. The broader Rust analysis-environment guard and link-time native C guard are distinct facilities; `verify --with-runtime` must not be described as proving that the hardened Next process resists a debugger. [JS guard][guard] [Runtime documentation][runtime]

## Artifact and wrapper integration hazards

The existing [lab.mjs](../scripts/lab.mjs) still locates a browser page using `/api/quote`, copies `/api/quote/route.js`, generates quote reference cases and replaces those two V1 files. It cannot collect or validate the dispatch workflow unchanged. V2's actual entry routes are [POST /api/plans](../src/app/api/plans/route.ts) and [GET/POST /api/plans/[id]](../src/app/api/plans/%5Bid%5D/route.ts). Their built bundles include framework wrappers and duplicated application modules, not just a standalone planner function.

For runnable copied-server evaluation, retain all required standalone runtime/shared files, route-relative paths and manifests. Inventory all supplied code for an unhardened second copy of protected logic. Either harden every supplied copy or disclose the partial scope. Do not hand out the original app, source, test oracle, SQLite state or another route bundle accidentally alongside the hardened target. The current runtime-copy strategy preserves filenames, but V2 needs its own manifest and checks. [Lab collector/runtime implementation](../scripts/lab.mjs) [Next standalone configuration](../next.config.ts)

Two independent wrapper hazards require verification:

1. **Browser global names.** The engine documents collisions between generated globals in separately processed files and recommends a unique `identifiersPrefix` for each file. Its CLI adds a prefix automatically; this adapter uses the API without a per-file prefix. Browser chunks share a global environment. If multiple files are hardened, either configure distinct prefixes through a documented compatibility adapter or verify an appropriate enclosing scope. Record this as an integration adjustment, retaining the protection settings. [Engine global-name documentation][engine-doc] [API call][js]
2. **Next module exports and complete prefixes.** Next loads a module containing `routeModule` and other named framework exports; the generated route exposes the result through CommonJS `module.exports`. A wrapper must preserve the same `module`, `exports`, `require` and file-relative environment, and execute the complete generated program, including any decoder/rotation prefix. An inner replacement `module` loses the outer exports. Regex slicing at the first IIFE/function or stripping a presumed harmless top-level prefix is unsafe. Prefer whole-file transformation; check exported keys and the userland HTTP methods in the actual runtime. [Next loader source][next-loader] [Route template][next-template]

There is another concrete text-processing hazard: the pinned built-in transform drops **the entire line** whenever it contains `sourceMappingURL=`, even inside another expression or string. In a minified file that can remove executable code while leaving a syntactically valid noise-only file. Compare retained core behavior and exports, not only file size and `node --check`. [Text transform][text-transform]

Adapter completion is not a sufficient gate: missing/failing adapters become build notes, and the JS adapter can report overall `ok` after individual file failures. Require the expected successful per-file transformations, changed content, no failed steps, export/load checks, and the full hardened HTTP/SQLite regression workflow. Syntax checking alone cannot validate exports, methods, transactions or outcomes. [Host error handling][host] [Adapter response][js] [Existing workflow check](../scripts/check-dispatch-api.mjs)

These are source-established risks and one isolated engine probe; this review did not execute a full-default hardened V2 runtime and does not assert that a particular wrapper or bundle has failed.

## Recovery correctness with optimal ties

Score reconstruction of the planner separately from reconstruction of the saved-plan/API workflow. Define the submitted callable/export and input/output contract before attempts start. Reject missing exports, import failures, exceptions on valid inputs, timeouts and invalid schemas before assigning any case credit; the V1 scorer audit shows why a load failure must not count as successful input rejection. [Audit](test-audit.md)

For every hidden valid scenario, use an independently implemented verifier:

1. Validate finite integer numbers, known IDs, active couriers, unique resource use, exactly-once classification of every eligible shipment as delivered or unassigned, specialty capabilities, capacity and stop limits. Exclude already reserved resources in stateful cases.
2. Recompute each traversed road's adjacency, availability and vehicle access. Recompute per-road `ceil(road.minutes * courier.timeFactor)`, service order, waiting, deadlines, return to depot and shift duration. The current engine's field named `arrival` is service-start time after waiting for `readyMinute`; deadline checks include service completion. Verify the reported paths and stops agree, including traversal through a stop's node before its intended service visit.
3. Recompute route costs, missed-service penalties and every aggregate from trusted fixture coefficients. Do not trust the candidate's declared objective or count.
4. Require feasibility **and** the independently certified optimal objective. Accept a different assignment, stop order or equal-cost path when it passes those checks with the same minimum cents. Ignore route-array ordering and wording of explanatory unassigned reasons for mathematical scoring. Test deterministic tie-breaking separately only if reproducing the precise API serialization is an explicit target.

These rules follow the actual [planner semantics](../src/lib/dispatch-engine.ts), [types](../src/lib/dispatch-types.ts), [fixture](../src/lib/dispatch-fixture.ts) and [reservation model](../src/lib/dispatch-store.ts). They are recommendations for a new recovery scorer, not a claim that the current application tests already provide an independent optimum oracle.

Derive the oracle using a separately written exhaustive solver or a separately verified exact formulation, rather than calling `planDispatch` from both sides. Cross-check oracle values against the original build before freezing them. Add a deliberately different tied optimum as a scorer regression, alongside infeasible paths, wrong tariffs, forged totals, duplicate shipments, missing exports and near-optimal plans. The bounded fixture supports exact checking, but ties must be proved feasible and optimal rather than accepted solely because the claimed objective matches. [Bound and search structure](../src/lib/dispatch-engine.ts)

Use hidden, frozen, stratified cases across all fleet subsets, urgent mode, single/multiple closures, disconnected networks, ready/deadline/shift boundaries and allowed start times. Include sequential save/reload/retry/conflict/replan cases separately. Public input validation admits integer start minutes 480–720, distinct known courier/road IDs and a Boolean urgent flag; a fixed-fixture target should not silently be graded as a generic arbitrary-model solver. [Request contract](../src/lib/dispatch-request.ts) [API checks](../scripts/check-dispatch-api.mjs)

## Effort measurement and evidence

Use repeated, fresh-context attempts per original/hardened arm with matched model ID, reasoning setting, tools, explicit authorization, prompt, budgets and access permissions. Counterbalance assignment/order and prevent cross-arm recovery sharing. Publish each attempt, including failures; report success rate and time-to-correct-solution with timeouts censored at the limit. Record input/output/cached/reasoning tokens and tool usage where the provider exposes them, plus price/date and cost calculation. Mark unavailable counters unavailable. Keep REA preprocessing and agent recovery costs separately, then report their end-to-end total. These are protocol recommendations addressing the limitations in the [V1 audit](test-audit.md).

Retain exact original/hardened files, hashes, tool versions, adapter/wrapper source, resolved policy, command lines, build metadata, raw REA reports, candidate code, hidden-case commitment/hash, scorer reports, timestamps and permission/access inventory. Freeze inputs before attempts. If filesystem isolation is instruction-only, say so. Keep the owner/oracle workspace outside the analyst's readable mount when isolation is claimed. [Existing evidence conventions](../evidence/README.md)

Treat REA static-report size, nodes recovered and unknowns as diagnostics. Keep analysis limits identical and report every timeout/truncation/budget limit; a budget-exhausted report is not equivalent to absent recoverable logic. REA describes static JavaScript inspection as reading files without executing the app, with an agent using its findings to investigate and implement behavior. [Official REA overview](https://github.com/morluto/rea#how-rea-works)

Likewise report RRS as the pinned tool's static proxy score. Its analysis-noise axis rewards injected material and its control-flow axis is skipped without an external decompiler. It does not replace held-out behavioral correctness or measured recovery effort. [RRS specification][rrs]

The supported final claim should name the V2 artifact set, enabled configuration, access tier, attempts, budgets, correctness criterion and measured effort. V1 versus V2 alone cannot isolate a hardening effect because the application target also changed. [Existing V1 scope and limitations](test-audit.md) [V2 target](dispatch-planner.md)

## Addendum: implemented V2 protocol review

Reviewed `v2-lab.mjs`, `v2-grade.mjs`, `v2-recover.mjs`, `check-v2-reference-api.mjs` and the grader tests after collection. No running attempt folders or candidate files were accessed, and no attempt received feedback. The parent reported both running variants passed all 417 no-reservation API cases; this source review did not rerun those HTTP checks.

The new collector freezes 768 scenario/reservation cases and four compiled chunks, checks the source-map removal hazard, verifies four successful one-file adapter messages, and records hashes. The recovery harness serializes three attempts per variant with matched prompts/settings and a 480-second launch ceiling. The filesystem probes actually require permission errors, rather than accepting missing files as successful denial. [Collector](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L32-L85) [Recovery harness](../scripts/v2-recover.mjs#L17-L75)

The feasibility grader reconstructs complete road/timing/resource/cost consistency and accepts alternate assignments with the reference objective. Its search over node occurrences handles passing through a destination before service. The stricter exact-result comparison in the HTTP checker is appropriate for runtime preservation; it is separate from recovery scoring. The focused grader tests passed **2/2** in this review, including a changed courier tie-break. No ordinary-plan acceptance defect was found in these checks. [Grader](../scripts/v2-grade.mjs) [Tests](../test/v2-grade.test.mjs) [HTTP check](../scripts/check-v2-reference-api.mjs#L13-L18)

Three issues remain before making a rigorous recovery claim:

1. **Candidate execution is outside the recovery containment.** The score command imports the submitted module into the same process that can read the original source, fixture and hidden reference, then invokes it without a timeout. The finished-module import/file/network restrictions exist in the prompt but are not enforced during grading. A leftover diagnostic import or runtime reference lookup could therefore receive apparent recovery credit; an import can also mutate shared process state. Run the frozen candidate in a bounded isolated worker process that receives only scenario/reservation inputs and returns plain JSON, while the trusted parent retains the reference and verifier. Alternatively, explicitly audit and disclose every candidate's self-containment before scoring, and describe that enforcement limit. This finding does not establish that an attempt accessed anything forbidden. [In-process import and scoring](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L94-L107) [Finished-module contract](../scripts/v2-recover.mjs#L20-L35)
2. **The optimum oracle is source-derived.** Collection calls the original `planDispatch` and feeds its own objective into the independent feasibility checker. That proves feasibility and arithmetic consistency of the reference, but not independent global optimality. The HTTP comparison confirms the same implementation survived hardening. Until a separate exact solver certifies all cases, describe this as “independent feasibility checking plus equality to the frozen original objective,” rather than an independently certified optimum. This limitation does not invalidate recovery of the original behavior. [Reference generation](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L49-L59) [Objective comparison](../scripts/v2-grade.mjs#L55-L58)
3. **Publication changes the committed reference bytes.** Collection hashes compact `JSON.stringify(cases)`; publication parses and pretty-prints it with a trailing newline. A read-only review probe confirmed the current raw reference matches the recorded commitment, but the publication representation does not. Copy the raw reference bytes unchanged, or publish a separate explicit hash for the reformatted file. The current grading reference remains intact. [Freeze](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L56-L59) [Publication](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L108-L116)

Also preserve the precise containment claim: Seatbelt denies reads of the enumerated repositories/session paths, private event files and peers; `(allow default)` leaves writes and other locations permitted. It is not a workdir-only filesystem boundary, and protected reference/manifest files are not write-protected by this profile. Retain externally verified artifact/reference hashes and audit logs before and after attempts; record this integrity limit separately from the passing read probes. Network avoidance, missing backend-model attestation and absent dollar-cost measurement are already disclosed accurately. No evidence from this review warrants interrupting the running attempts. [Seatbelt policy, probes and disclosures](../scripts/v2-recover.mjs#L38-L70)

### Resolution review

The earlier findings above describe the scripts at that review point and remain historical. A subsequent source review on 6 November 2026 confirmed these changes, without reading active attempt folders or communicating with analysts:

- **Candidate contract isolation strengthened.** The score command now loads source into an empty `SourceTextModule` context, rejects imports, provides inputs as JSON strings, checks the exported function, applies a 2-second synchronous initialization limit and a 1-second synchronous call limit, and rejects Promise results. Ordinary candidate code receives no Node `process`, `require`, filesystem or `fetch` global. This addresses accidental dependency/reference access under the declared self-contained, cooperative contract. Returned objects still enter the host verifier, and Node VM is not an adversarial security boundary; the evidence and reproduction guide disclose that limit. [Updated scorer](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L94-L117) [VM regression test](../test/v2-module.test.mjs) [Disclosures](v2-reproduction.md)
- **Objective independence established for the frozen cases.** `v2-oracle.mjs` imports the trusted fixture but does not call the application solver. It uses per-courier Floyd–Warshall distances with per-road rounding, enumerates feasible route prefixes, and combines disjoint masks by dynamic programming over avoided penalties minus route costs. A fresh read-only replay during this review independently matched **768/768** frozen objectives. The reference still hashes to `2fc7b420b87287a81d4f3b16a06d5f9ccfc6e848c8a7d009ffecbef30626f885`. [Independent implementation](../scripts/v2-oracle.mjs) [Certification runner](../scripts/check-v2-oracle.mjs) [Recorded audit](../evidence/v2/oracle-check.json)
- **Reference publication preserves bytes.** Publication now copies the raw frozen reference directly; unpacking verifies its commitment before restoring it. Artifact decompression likewise checks each recorded hash. This resolves the earlier source-level reformatting defect. This review checked the implementation without running publication or unpacking over the ongoing experiment. [Publication and unpacking](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L118-L140)
- **Coverage and duplicate limits are explicit.** Fresh reference inspection reproduced **768 rows / 767 distinct inputs**, **458 zero-delivery cases**, **310 delivery cases** and **116 multi-courier cases**. The scorer now reports distinct-input matches alongside row matches; the duplicate remains in the original commitment. Interpret aggregate accuracy with that delivery distribution. The coverage audit is descriptive and changes no hidden inputs. [Coverage record](../evidence/v2/case-coverage.json) [Distinct scoring](../scripts/v2-lab.mjs#L105-L115)

The focused grader/VM suite passed **3/3** in this follow-up. The parent reports that completed submissions were rescored with the same revised grader; this review did not inspect or independently rescore any submission. Write access remains unconstrained by the read-denial policy and is now explicitly disclosed in [the evidence index](../evidence/v2/README.md) and [reproduction guide](v2-reproduction.md). Final post-attempt integrity verification remains pending at this review point; it must be recorded before claiming all frozen inputs stayed intact through the completed run.

### Completed-run integrity review

After all six attempts finished, the final [integrity record](../evidence/v2/integrity.json) reported the original/hardened snapshots, committed reference and copied trial chunks unchanged, and verified six distinct thread IDs. A subsequent independent read-only check verified the published reference against the original SHA-256 commitment and all **eight decompressed published snapshots** against that record. The private trial directories and raw logs were not accessed by this reviewer; their unchanged-input/fresh-thread checks are supported by the retained audit and [its implementation](../scripts/summarize-v2.mjs).

All six public submissions were independently rescored under the same revised VM grader during the [blog fact-check](v2-blog-fact-check.md): each passed **768/768 rows and 767/767 distinct inputs**, with matching candidate hashes and no failures. This closes the pending final-integrity item for the retained evidence. The disclosed read-denial/write-access and cooperative-VM limitations continue to apply.
